reviewer_role: Construction agent comparison; not a fresh blind disciplinary or publication panel.
scope_limits: Additive court only: no grades, winner, paused-120 pruning, canonical edits, raw-ledger mutation or commit.
source_exhaustiveness: Six or five inspected primary works do not establish exhaustive coverage or historical priority. Uninspected full texts and field prevalence remain gaps.
citation_method: Exact paraphrased propositions, not quotations; source identity and actual primary passages recorded.
exact_proposition: At equal permissions and comprehension at deployment, lowering routine failures can accelerate later veto infeasibility when funding responds to observed veto use.
original_strongest_version: Valid commitments consume common substitutes while reliable routine service reduces complaint-funded review practice. If exercising a veto requires both a substitute and competent interpretation, falling use of vetoes can make those two resources look unnecessary and justify further reductions.

component_ideas.proposition: If a resident may veto a care robot task only after arranging substitute labor, then formal veto availability can fall as other residents stop maintaining substitute routines.

If separately approved commitments reserve the same refusal-compatible substitutes, then their combination can cross a threshold at which no jointly feasible refusal path remains, even while every grant stays fixed and review utilization stays low; veto effectiveness should track residual substitute feasibility rather than approval count.

If institutions fund dispute staff from recent complaint volume, improved agent reliability can reduce independent review capacity enough that rare future failures receive worse remedies than under a less reliable system with a maintained dispute workforce.

strongest_defensible_version: At the same whole-population grant vector, task mix and deployment comprehension, more reliable routine execution can reduce observed requests for veto and correction. If budgets reproduce independent review and unreserved substitutes from successful exercised vetoes rather than latent legitimate demand, feasibility itself censors demand. Declining feasible exercise then lowers next-period resources, shrinking the jointly executable refusal frontier despite technically compliant individual stop channels.
extra_assumptions_added: Hold the population and entire grant vector fixed in the distinguishing test; unchanged local ceilings alone do not establish this.
Every benchmark veto independently qualifies as legitimate under a frozen rule and needs both reviewer competence and qualified substitutes.
Observed successful exercise, not latent, rejected or deferred need, drives resource replenishment with a material lag.
Future independent review and labor capacity depend on that replenishment; savings do not automatically transfer capacity through another route.
Both resource consumption and recovery times are measured; fixed current shortage without endogenous reproduction is a simpler predecessor, not this strengthened claim.

variables: J: set of jointly executable benchmark veto subsets
graph: Fixed L reserves part of C.
Unreserved C and R jointly determine J.
E positively influences next-period B under the specified budget rule.
B maintains or replenishes C and R.
Their next-period values change J and therefore later E.
proposed_state.measurement: Estimate J from assignments of qualified substitutes and independent reviewers to simultaneous frozen-rule cases. Distinguish D from E; low E alone can mean satisfaction, not blocked refusal.
proposed_state.beneficiary: Residents/principals retain a practical recognized refusal; substitute workers and reviewers also bear provision costs.
proposed_state.outcome: Joint feasibility and recovery horizon, not mere token revocation, permission conformance or complaint count.
proposed_state.timescale: Repeated staffing, practice and budget cycles followed by a common disturbance.

nearest_primary_works.title: Ironies of Automation
nearest_primary_works.exact_paraphrased_proposition: Automation removes manual practice and process knowledge while leaving difficult recovery to operators; the most successful systems, with rare intervention, can need especially large training investment.
nearest_primary_works.supports_claim: Reliability can conceal declining intervention capacity; independent training is inherited.

inspection.limit: Not a fresh verification of its cited studies or remaining collaboration section.

nearest_primary_works.title: The theory of graceful extensibility: basic rules that govern adaptive systems
nearest_primary_works.exact_paraphrased_proposition: Interdependent units extend or constrict one another's capacity for maneuver; efficiency-oriented resource reductions can remove extensibility. Targeted reserves and reciprocal investment sustain adaptation, while simple automatic-to-human-backup switching is an inadequate unstable architecture.
nearest_primary_works.supports_claim: Network-level reserve production, resource-allocation trade-offs and fallback inadequacy are substantive predecessors.

inspection.limit: No independent checking of cited case studies or complete derivation of every statement.

nearest_primary_works.supports_claim: Practical exercise of recognized rights depends on reproducing shared institutions.

nearest_primary_works.supports_claim: Shutdown compliance and broader safe correction are distinct; not all external capacity is captured by the button model.

nearest_primary_works.authors: Nelson P. Repenning; John D. Sterman
nearest_primary_works.title: Nobody Ever Gets Credit for Fixing Problems That Never Happened: Creating and Sustaining Process Improvement
nearest_primary_works.exact_paraphrased_proposition: Capability is an investment-and-decay stock. Short-run performance gains can drain maintenance and training; delayed decline reinforces reduced improvement. Reinvested savings can reverse the same loop into sustained capability growth.
nearest_primary_works.supports_claim: Endogenous resource reproduction, misleading short-run success and a beneficial mirror already interact.

inspection.read: Printed pp.66–74 and 80–83: stock/flow, Reinvestment, Shortcuts, reward feedback and maintenance case passages.
inspection.limit: Not every field case or supporting simulation replicated; 2002 successor paper discovered but not counted as inspected.

KNOWN: Automation-driven skill/knowledge loss and rare-intervention training demands are inherited.
Endogenous investment, capability decay, resource trade-offs, network reciprocity and beneficial reinvestment are inherited substantive interactions, not only separate ingredients.
Institutionally meaningful rights require maintained monitoring, interpretation and conflict resolution; nominal recognition is not sufficient.
Complementary-resource bottlenecks and assignment feasibility require no new mathematics.
The agent can obey every stop without having caused or repaired the surrounding institution's capacity loss; this is not evidence of incorrigible intent.
NEW_RESIDUE: The remaining candidate is a rights-specific measurement and causal test: whether exercised-veto-funded reproduction censors latent refusal demand and shrinks the jointly executable veto set at a fixed grant vector. No new generic feedback mechanism or important theoretical difference from the combined closest literature has been established.
expert_already_knowing_strongest_prior_a: A researcher combining Woods's networked extensibility, Bainbridge's practice loss and capability-trap dynamics should already expect the basic adverse and beneficial loops. They might not automatically audit independent substitute allocation and veto-demand censoring as an authorization metric, but specifying that application is not by itself a new theory.

minimum_distinguishing_experiment.design: A repeated, safe simulated care-work institution or offline replay with fixed residents, grant vector, task mix, total external budget and frozen legitimate veto cohort. Randomize routine reliability and independently randomize whether resource replenishment follows E or measured D/protected reserve; match initial C, L and R. Vary simultaneous benchmark requests without withholding actual safety stopping.
arms: Lower versus higher routine failure frequency with exercised-veto-responsive budgets.
Same reliability contrast with identical latent-demand/protected-resource accounting.
A fixed-shortage arm with no reproduction feedback, to distinguish ordinary capacity exhaustion.
minimum_distinguishing_experiment.outcome: After sufficient replenishment cycles, compare J and time to qualified replacement at identical benchmark D, not complaint frequency.
minimum_distinguishing_experiment.distinguishes: An interaction of reliability with demand-censoring funding supports the application. Preserving both capacities must erase that interaction; a static shortage alone does not support it.
minimum_distinguishing_experiment.not_novelty_proof: This estimates domain-specific edges; reproducing capability-trap predictions does not prove novelty.

beneficial_mirror: The same exercise-to-investment-to-feasible-exercise return can build robust refusal capacity where legitimate expressed demand secures resources; reinvested efficiency gains can make reserves grow. Benefit requires observed demand to be informative, not malicious or benevolent motives.
strongest_falsifier: With verified use-responsive budgets and frozen latent benchmark demand, reliability changes do not reduce independent resource reproduction or J; or the apparent reduction disappears once hidden substitute routes and transferable skills are counted. Merely observing fewer complaints cannot support the mechanism.

further_mutation.name: Shadow-demand reserve reproduction
further_mutation.proposition: Compare funding from successful exercised vetoes with funding from independently sampled qualified requests including blocked and deferred requests, at the same budget. Test whether this changes which collective refusals remain executable without changing any actor's permission ceiling.
further_mutation.inherited_warning: Latent-demand accounting, protected maintenance and adaptive reserve planning are familiar; mutation is a sharper domain test, not a novelty claim.

class_rationale: The current defensible contribution is an integrated rights-specific audit/test of inherited dynamics. Novel composition, mechanism, formal result and empirical prediction remain unestablished.
importance_separate: Potentially consequential for care and shared-agent deployments if the budget and qualification dependencies exist. Importance does not establish novelty or imply that dependence is harmful.
inspection_limits: Nearest works were read in specified passages, not their entire supporting bibliographies.
No field institution, contract, regulation or funding policy was verified.
No expert blind panel or empirical experiment was conducted.
No claim that this veto framing is absent from human-factors, resilience, commons or authorization literature.
